name: Hakkoz
overview: Hakkoz was a male Levite who served as the seventh priest chosen among the twenty-four priestly courses established during King David's time. He was in the priestly line of Eleazar, a significant branch of the tribe of Levi. Despite his distinguished role, some of Hakkoz's descendants later faced challenges in proving their priestly lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Hakkoz means "the thorn," as recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:10. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God but identifies this individual within the priestly divisions.
familyAndRelationships: Hakkoz is noted as a descendant of Eleazar, linking him to a prominent priestly family within the tribe of Levi. Beyond this connection, Scripture does not record additional family relationships for Hakkoz.
scriptureSignificance: Hakkoz holds significance in the biblical narrative as one of the twenty-four priestly courses established to organize the service of the temple. His placement as the seventh course highlights the structured nature of Levitical ministry under David's reforms. The mention of his descendants' inability to prove their lineage in Nehemiah underscores the ongoing importance of genealogical records for priestly legitimacy in Israel.
